blockers.message: the review record has no `## code.review` section, while roles were active at it
R-ops-1 (The switch to Paylane has no way back) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-ops-2 (Nobody sees the settlement worker fail or not run) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence:
The Stripe client is deleted and replaced by the Paylane client in the same
release. There is no switch between the two: keeping both would double the
code to maintain. The Stripe account is closed the day after the release.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: All traffic moves at deploy
findings.recommendation: Keep a way back until Paylane has proven itself in production: either keep the Stripe client behind a configuration switch (provider selected per environment, flippable without a release), or at least keep the Stripe account open for a stated rollback window (several weekly release cycles) so that deploying the previous version still processes payments. Close the account in a later change, once the window has passed. Say in the design how a rollback is done and who decides it. Scenario that fails: on day 2 Paylane rejects or times out on a share of authorizations; the previous release still calls Stripe, but the Stripe account is closed, so a redeploy cannot restore card payments, and the next fix waits for the weekly release.
findings.title: The switch to Paylane has no way back

findings.evidence:
A new worker, `settlement-worker`, runs at 02:00, fetches the day's Paylane
payments and matches them to orders. It runs as a Kubernetes CronJob and
writes its result to the database.
findings.location: design.md#Decision: A worker settles payments nightly
findings.recommendation: Decide in the design how an operator learns that a run failed or never happened: alert on a failed CronJob (or on the absence of a successful run by a set hour), log a structured start and end of each run with the counts fetched, matched and unmatched, and expose the last successful run time. Add a requirement and a scenario for a failed run (Paylane unreachable, database error) next to "A payment without order". Scenario that fails: the Paylane API is down at 02:00 or the job crashes; the CronJob fails, no row is written and no alert is sent — the finance alert only fires for a payment without order in a successful run — so unsettled payments go unnoticed for days.
findings.title: Nobody sees the settlement worker fail or not run
